title: Planting and harvesting
intro: Every farm starts with dirt under your nails. Here's how I did it.
bullets: Tap empty soil to pick a seed. It stays picked, so drag across more plots to plant them all.
Planted the wrong thing? Tap it again within 3 seconds and you get your coins back.
Ripe crops wave at you. Tap or drag across them to harvest.
Pick crops soon after they ripen for a Fresh Pick: a coin tip and extra XP. Wait too long and the bonus is gone.
Replant All, at the start of the seed tray, puts the same crops back in every empty plot.

title: Selling: crate, market and board
intro: Where you sell matters more than what you grow. I learned that the slow way.
bullets: The shipping crate in the Barn pays 70% of a crop's value. Quick, but the worst price in town.
Board orders pay the most. Keep what an order wants, sell the rest.

bullets.text: Pip's market in Town pays 80% to 140% of value, and never less than the crate.
Market prices change every 8 hours: midnight, 8 am and 4 pm. If today's price is low, it may be better later.
The featured crop always pays 165%, the best price at the market. It changes with the prices.

bullets: When the barn is full, crops ship themselves at crate price. Sell before that happens.

title: Board orders and Specials
intro: Neighbours pin what they need on the Board. Treat it like a shopping list that pays you.
bullets: A new order goes up every 2 hours, even while you're away. Orders never expire.
Pass on an order you don't like. It's free, and a new one comes on the next tick.

bullets.text: The gold Daily Special asks for three things and pays a Ribbon. Hand in each line as you get it.

bullets: Filling orders makes friends, too. Every order adds to that villager's hearts.

title: Planning around your day
intro: Crops grow while you sleep. A good farmer plants for the next time they'll look.
bullets: Before you put the phone down, plant something that will be ready when you come back.
Short crops while you're playing, long crops overnight or during work.
A crop left ripe for hours is fine, but you miss its Fresh Pick bonus.
Longer crops earn more per harvest. Faster ones earn more per hour, if you're around to replant.

title: Growing your farm
intro: I let half the land go wild. Win it back a plot at a time.
bullets: Tap weeds, branches and rocks to clear them. Branches give wood, rocks give stone.
Bruno's crew clears stumps and boulders past the fence, one plot at a time, if you pay them.

bullets.text: Better soil grows crops faster, and rich soil sometimes gives an extra crop.

bullets: Fertilizer doubles one harvest. Save it for your most valuable crops.

title: Buildings and goods
intro: A sack of flour sells for far more than the wheat that went into it.
bullets: Buildings turn crops into goods. Goods are worth more than the crops they're made from.
Start a batch, then come back. Buildings work while you're away, too.
Board orders and the story often ask for goods. Keep a few on hand.
Ribbons buy extra slots, so a building can work on more at once.

title: Friends and gifts
intro: Bramblewick is small. Everybody remembers who was kind.
bullets: Gifts, orders and quests all add hearts. Each villager has favourite things; loved gifts count the most.
At 3 and 6 hearts a villager shares a moment with you, and a Ribbon or two.
At 5 hearts each friend gives you a lasting perk.
Each villager takes one gift a day.

title: Ziggy's cart
intro: Ziggy sells everything and explains nothing. Buy anyway.
bullets: Ziggy's cart comes to town every few days. A badge on Town tells you when.
He brings seeds you can't grow yet, plus wood, stone, gold and fertilizer.
Early seeds are pricey, but they can open up a better crop days ahead of time.

title: Hazel's Almanac and mastery
intro: Hazel knows plants better than I ever did. Listen to her.
bullets: Every crop earns stars the more you grow it. Each star pays a Ribbon and a bonus.
Pick Coins, XP, Quick Growth, Bountiful or Thrifty. Coins is the safe pick; the others suit how you play.
Once a week you can redo one crop's stars for free, from its page in the Almanac.
Ten stars earns a gold page and a sparkle in the field.

title: Meadow visitors
intro: Bugs aren't pests. Mostly. Hazel will tell you which.
bullets: Little visitors land on your crops while they grow, even while you're away.
Tap one to sketch it for the Sketchbook and collect pollen.
Five pollen makes a honey. Honey is worth a lot, and neighbours ask for it.
Some visitors only come to certain crops. Grow a mix.

title: Creek fishing
intro: I used to fish the creek every evening. Nell still does.
bullets: Bites build up while you're away. Come by and catch them.
Cast, wait for the bobber to dip, then tap Reel. Missing a fish costs nothing.
Different fish bite at different times of day.
Fish make good gifts and fill some orders.

title: Town projects
intro: Bramblewick gets back on its feet one project at a time.
bullets: Every week the town asks for some crops and coins. Finish it for Ribbons and a trophy.
Each town level raises the price of everything you sell.
Big projects like the bridge give the whole farm a lasting perk.

title: Ribbons
intro: Ribbons are the town's way of saying well done. Coins can't buy them.
bullets: You get Ribbons for new crops, mastery stars, heart moments, Daily Specials and town projects.
Spend them on extra building slots, so a building can work on more at once.
